```text
Peak Poker Performance

operate at the wrong degree of action. They do nothing, give up easily, or
take normal levels of action. Naturally, he encourages taking massive
amounts of action, and the easiest way to get into action regularly is to
create systems and habits.
    If you want to be average, you don’t need to worry too much about
the habits and systems that you create for yourself. But if you want to
achieve peak performance, you need to look at which activities give you
the best odds of being successful and do those every day (or as often as
possible). Most people rely on willpower to force them to do what they
need to do, but it is infinitely easier to establish habits and systems that
run on autopilot. Willpower is limited, so anything you can do to reduce
your reliance on it is going to benefit you. Mark Zuckerberg, the founder
of Facebook, has dozens of the same gray t-shirts, because he has more
important things to think about than what he’s going to wear each day.
Scott Adams, the creator of Dilbert, says that he never wastes a brain cell
in the morning deciding what he’s going to do because he just works his
system. Find ways to put as much of your life on autopilot as you can so
you can focus on what’s really important to you.
    To decide what habits and systems you need to install, think about
what a perfect playing session looks like for you. If I could wave a magic
wand that would make every session you play a masterpiece, how would
that look? Think about everything that would contribute to you playing
your absolute best from a very high level. What time do you get up? Do
you exercise before playing? How much? What about meditation? Do
certain foods energize you? Leave no stone unturned and once you come
up with a clear idea of the exact variables that help you play your best,
make habits and systems out of those behaviors. A great year comes
from having a series of great days, so do everything you can to make
every day a masterpiece.
```

```text
                                                               Introduction

      Believing that your qualities are carved in stone – the fixed
      mindset – creates an urgency to prove yourself over and
      over. If you have only a certain amount of intelligence, a cer-
      tain personality, and a certain moral character – well, then
      you’d better prove that you have a healthy dose of them. It
      simply wouldn’t do to look or feel deficient in these most basic
      characteristics.

   Having a fixed mindset makes us scared to try new things and keeps us
stuck. Contrast this with what she says about the growth mindset:

      In this mindset, the hand you’re dealt is just the starting point
      for development. The growth mindset is based on the belief
      that your basic qualities are things you can cultivate through
      your efforts. Although people may differ in every which way –
      in their initial talents and aptitudes, interests, or tempera-
      ments – everyone can change and grow through application
      and experience.

   Being willing to look at each hand as a little experiment that offers data
to be used to improve our strategy epitomizes a growth mindset. Always
ask yourself, “What could I have done better?” or “How could I have re-
sponded that would have been better?” It’s important that you do these
exercises without criticizing or judging yourself harshly. As you will see
later in the book, those are negative psychological activities, which im-
pede progress. Your goal is to know that every experience at the table is
simple data to be used to get better. Your goal: to get a little bit better
each time you play. Do this with every session and see what happens. I
think you will be pleased.
```

```text
Principle 6: Master Your Mindset
As you will learn later in the book, a revolution is under way in peak per-
formance psychology that is squarely focused on mindset improvements.
The strategy of mindfulness has been shown in hundreds of studies to be
an effective mechanism for improving mindset.
   Currently, mindfulness-based approaches are being used by athletes,
military and law enforcement personnel, stock traders, chess players,
corporate executives and, of course, poker players. Mindfulness medita-
tion has the power to give you a centeredness that allows you to step
outside of your ego to look at things without getting overly emotional. It
has also been shown to increase focus and attention and improve overall
mood.
   Later in the book, I’ll share specific approaches, practices, and tech-
niques that will help you build your mindfulness skills. If you would like to
manage your emotions and thoughts more effectively, reduce impulsive
behavior that is not useful, and increase the quality of your decision mak-
ing at the table, I encourage you to give mindfulness-based strategies a
try.
```

```text
Peak Poker Performance

Principle 7: Understand and Optimize Your Brain
The most potent performance enhancer you have is the three pounds of
gray matter located between your eyes. It is more powerful than any su-
per computer, and if you use the methods outlined in this book, you can
expect to improve your performance by a wide margin.
    Thanks to imaging technologies, we now know more about the brain
than we ever have before. Not too many years ago we thought that the
brain was fixed once you reached adulthood. Fortunately, we know now
that the brain is “plastic”: as long as you provide it with the proper inputs,
it will continue to grow and develop.
    If you want to truly flourish, pay special attention to your brain. It con-
trols every thought, emotion, feeling, sensation, urge, and behavior that
you produce. If you want to understand why you react to tilt, down-
swings, variance, or even rushes, the brain provides answers. Understand-
ing how your brain evolved and why it works the way it does can give you
great insights into your actions and reactions.
    I urge you to pay close attention to the chapters on the brain, because
the decisions you make every minute of everyday are shaping and mold-
ing your brain whether you know it or not. Your brain is either spiraling up
and improving and growing or spiraling down and shrinking. Fun fact: your
brain starts shrinking on the order of 5% per decade once you reach the
age of 30 unless you take steps to stop it. Since the brain is your most
important tool at the table, I encourage you to pay close attention to it!

Principle 8: A Willingness to
Develop Your Full Potential
I work with a lot of players who are actively seeking out peak perform-
ance. They look for opportunities and when they see one, they are com-
pelled to make the mental, physical, and personal sacrifices necessary to
take advantage. Being good is not good enough; they want to be great.
   I coach people on how to manage their mindset so that they can do
what they already do well better. I don’t create talent; you have to do
that yourself; but I help players achieve their potential. This book is about
how to become a better poker player and a more fully actualized person.
```

```text
                                                                  Introduction

The people I work with are all already extremely good at what they do.
But they aren’t satisfied with being good. They want to stretch them-
selves so that they are great. They are committed to doing whatever it
takes to reach greatness.
   If you want to become a great player, too, you must identify areas for
improvement, map out a plan of action, and find ways to be accountable
for taking the needed actions. The truly successful players are not super
human. In many cases, they are flawed (as we all are) but where they ex-
cel is in learning how to think and behave differently in certain key areas.
   To think like a peak performer, you have to get comfortable with the
idea of being uncomfortable. You have got to want success badly enough
that you stop making decisions based on emotions and stick to an optimal
strategy – even when it’s the last thing you want to do.
   Consider the following traits that are common to most of the top
poker players I consult with. They are:

    ♠ methodical and careful about making decisions
    ♠ extremely self-disciplined
    ♠ resilient to setbacks
    ♠ strongly committed to learning and growing
    ♠ able to see mistakes as opportunities to learn
    ♠ capable of leaving their ego at the door
    ♠ willing and able to pull the trigger on making big bets when the
        time is right
    ♠ capable of a high degree of self-awareness that allows them to
        make the most of their strengths and minimize the impact of their
        weaknesses.
   Every single thing on that list is a learnable skill that can be acquired and
applied by anyone. This book is filled with ideas and suggestions that you
can put into practice to increase every single one of the items on that list.
```

```text
Peak Poker Performance

    The most important question to ask yourself as you start your journey
through this book is: are you maximizing your full potential? Next, how
committed are you to being the best you can be? Are you willing to hold
yourself accountable for doing what needs to be done? This is what really
separates people. Stop letting your emotions determine your actions and
listen to what your data is telling you.
    Figure out what you have to in order to reach your highest level of
success and then do it – every single day. Your desire to be the best has
to outweigh your desire not to do the things that need to be done even
when doing so is boring or hard. Top performers make the conscious
choice to do the hard things. You may have good, justifiable reasons why
you are not putting in as much work as you need to. But the real reason
you aren’t sticking to your plans is because you haven’t yet found suffi-
cient motivation to do so. That’s why you must get clear on your vision
and why being the best you can be is important to you.
    I’m confident this book can help you optimize your thinking and deci-
sion-making processes if you are willing to approach it with an open atti-
tude. I am going to offer you some new ways to think about how you op-
erate both at the table and away from it. It’s easy to be caught up in the
stress of the moment and get distracted, but having some options that
you can experiment with can help you exponentially. If you are willing to
develop all the qualities listed in this book, I have no doubt you can make
more money and be more in control of your emotions. The characteristics
described in this book are those that differentiate mediocrity from great-
ness and greatness from superstardom.

Getting the Most from Peak Poker Performance
Most people come away from books and training programs with plenty of
new ideas but then they don’t actually implement most of them. A key
factor in whether or not this book will help you enhance your poker per-
formance will be how fully you immerse yourself in the book and take ac-
tion as a result of it. You’ll get out of it what you put into. Having said
that, here are a few tips that should help you increase its utility for you:
```

```text
   ♠ Keep in mind that enhancing performance is an evolutionary
```
